default.label: Opening
sentences: If you could be famous for anything in the world, what would you choose?
It's a question that tells you more about a person than almost any other — and the answer, I think, says everything about what we truly value.

default.label: Development 1
sentences: As far as I'm concerned, being famous for scientific discovery would be the greatest achievement imaginable.
One of the key things I love about science is how a single idea can change millions of lives — often long after the person who had it is gone.
If I had to choose one example, it would be someone like Marie Curie, celebrated not for fame itself, but for what she gave the world.

default.label: Development 2
sentences: Apart from the legacy it creates, another thing that really stands out about this kind of fame is how it inspires others.
What makes it so special is the ripple effect — every great scientist who becomes famous probably encourages dozens of young people to follow the same path.

default.label: Closing
sentences: In short, there's something truly unforgettable about people who are famous for making a genuine difference.
Whether you agree with my choice or not, there's no denying that lasting fame — the kind worth having — means leaving something meaningful behind long after the applause has faded.

sentences: Is there a place so beautiful, so full of life and history, that everyone deserves to see it at least once?
For me, the answer has always been the same: Sintra, a small town tucked into the hills just outside Lisbon.

default.label: Development 1
sentences: I'll never forget the time I first arrived there on a grey autumn morning.

What makes it so special is the way the palaces emerge from the hillside mist like something from a fairy tale — the vivid yellows and pinks of the Pena Palace against a sky full of low cloud is an image I will carry with me always.

topic.frame: I'll never forget the time when

sentences: For me personally, the best thing about Sintra is how it manages to feel both grand and intimate at the same time.
You can wander through royal gardens, stumble upon hidden chapels, and stop at a small café for a warm pastry, all within an hour.
Apart from its beauty, another thing that really stands out is how accessible it is — just forty minutes by train from Lisbon.

default.label: Opening
sentences: Why do so many students find it so difficult to stay healthy?
Between classes, deadlines, and a social life that seems to demand its own full-time schedule, it can feel almost impossible — but a few small changes really do make all the difference.

topic.frame: Why do so many people attach such importance to

default.label: Development 1
sentences: What makes the biggest difference, in my experience, is routine.
One of the key things I've learned is that eating proper meals instead of relying on snacks saves both time and energy — and your brain, it turns out, works considerably better when it's been fed.
If you often skip breakfast, try preparing something simple the night before.
It sounds obvious, but for most students it's genuinely transformative.

topic.frame: One of the key things I love about

default.label: Development 2
sentences: Apart from diet, another thing that really stands out is the power of walking.
You don't need a gym membership — walking to class, taking the stairs, or spending twenty minutes outside at lunchtime changes your mood in ways that a double espresso simply cannot match.

default.label: Closing
sentences: In short, staying healthy as a student isn't about dramatic lifestyle changes or expensive wellness routines.
Whether you start with sleep, food, or movement, there's no denying that small, consistent steps leave a lasting impression on how you feel — and ultimately, on how you perform.
